title: An already-present dep still fires an 'installed' toast on re-verify
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-467 (the 1.4 smoke umbrella) - surfaced by its GPU smoke matrix, listed in tasks/MPI-467/brief.md.

Observed during the MPI-467 GPU smoke matrix, 2026-08-08. The install leg re-verified 95 deps against a volume that ALREADY held all of them (aghcuvg7nl, 325 GB used, filled by the previous run), and the app fired a completion toast per model anyway: 'ILL Anime Beauty installed.', 'SDXL Realistic installed.', 'Download complete - SDXL NSFW installed.' Nothing was downloaded - the deps were present and the verify was a no-op.

User-facing, not smoke-only: any user who reconnects to a Pod whose volume is already full gets a wall of 'installed' toasts for downloads that never happened. It also devalues the toast, which is the only signal that a real install finished.

A dep that was already present should complete silently, or report as verified rather than installed. WHERE TO LOOK: the remote install completion path that emits the toast - it needs to distinguish 'downloaded now' from 'already there' before deciding to notify.

SECOND SYMPTOM, SAME ROOT, observed by the user 2026-08-09. The Model Library grid also shows a FILLED 100% progress bar on a model that is NOT installed on the active engine. He saw it on NVIDIA PiD Upscaler and Boogu Image Edit (BALANCED) while both cards still read INSTALL, and reasonably read it as "did you start downloading these to my drive?".

Nothing was downloading. /comfy/downloads/active answered {"models": [], "engine": false}, and none of the deps existed locally (searched for pid_sd3_1024_to_4096_4step_bf16.safetensors, boogu_image_edit_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors and gemma_2_2b_it_elm_bf16.safetensors across G:/CubricModels and %APPDATA%/Cubric Vision - all absent, which also matches the Load CLIP error the local bench threw). What the bars actually render is STALE COMPLETED-JOB STATE: /comfy/downloads/status still listed those install jobs at status "complete" from a REMOTE install leg that landed on the Pod volume, not on this disk. So the grid is drawing remote install progress against local availability.

That is the same "downloaded now vs already there" confusion as the toast, one layer up in the UI, and it should be fixed in the same pass: a completion record for another engine must not paint a local tile. Remote mode had since flipped to active:false (the app self-healed when its Pod went away), which is why the bars were left stranded with no engine behind them.
